title: Prevent stale Multi-Site health history from presenting a current crisis
opportunity: The browser Multi-Site view consumed the server isStale flag but ignored it when resolving an unknown live state, allowing an old critical trend to remain visible as a current crisis.
rootCause: displayHealthState used historical alertState without applying summary.isStale for unknown runtime health.
implementation: Added a stale display state and Thai explanation that explicitly says the summary is too old to confirm a crisis.
When live health is unknown and the summary is stale, the browser now renders stale instead of critical/degraded/healthy historical state.
Preserved current runtime healthy, unhealthy, invalid and pending-restart precedence.

tdd.red: BrowserMultiSiteStaleDisplayContractTests initially failed because the browser workflow did not inspect summary.isStale or provide stale copy.

verification.impeccableDetector: passed with four pre-existing advisory color findings (#ff4d5e, #22374f, #ff6378); no new finding
verification.uiAuditBoundary: browser copy/state refinement; no CSS/HTML visual assets changed; existing UI audit baseline retained

boundaries: Authenticated browser/published-EXE smoke, visual responsive verification, full VSTest testhost connectivity, live PostgreSQL behavior, CodeQL/SARIF, external penetration testing, load/SLO, SIEM, Authenticode signing, and production certification remain unverified.
